author: Mark Atwood
text:
Resolved via option B (document the version coupling), applied as a workspace-canonical sweep across all 8 extension-server crates.

## Why option B, not option A

The bead's primary recommendation (option A: delete the re-export) would break the documented public API contract:

- crate-jmap-chat-server/README.md:161-169 documents 'register_chat_handlers registers each method as a ClosureHandler ... If you need to register handlers individually via ClosureHandler ...' — i.e., ClosureHandler IS part of the consumer-facing API.
- crate-jmap-mail-server/README.md:178 + :261 carry the same documented surface.

Deleting the re-export silently would force consumers to add jmap-server as a direct dependency to write any additional handler. That's higher friction than a one-paragraph rustdoc explaining the version coupling.

## What I found in the workspace

All 8 extension-server crates carry the same 'pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler;' line:
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/lib.rs:272
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/lib.rs:293
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/lib.rs:230
- crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/lib.rs:135
- crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/lib.rs:116
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/lib.rs:141
- crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/lib.rs:160
- crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/lib.rs:116 (already had the stability doc-comment)

So sharing-server was the only one with the doc-comment — a sibling-leads-canonical drift that the canonical-template rule says to fix by propagating the existing wording to the canonical (mail-server) first, then to all other siblings.

## Fix applied

Lifted the existing sharing-server wording (verbatim except for the per-crate 'register_*_handlers' macro name) to mail-server first, then to chat/calendars/contacts/filenode/metadata/tasks. Each crate now carries the same rustdoc block:

  /// Generic closure-to-[`JmapHandler`] adapter from [`jmap_server`].
  ///
  /// Re-exported so the [`register_<extension>_handlers`] macro body can name
  /// `ClosureHandler` without a fully-qualified path. **Stability**: this
  /// re-export pins the major-version contract of [`jmap_server::ClosureHandler`]
  /// into this crate's public surface — a breaking change to that type
  /// upstream is a breaking change here. Consumers needing a closure handler
  /// adapter SHOULD prefer importing from [`jmap_server`] directly; the
  /// re-export is retained primarily for the in-crate macro and for
  /// backward-compatible spelling of the existing handler-registration
  /// pattern.

## Gates

- cargo check --workspace: clean
- cargo clippy -- -D warnings (7 modified crates): clean
- cargo test (7 modified crates): all passing
- cargo doc --no-deps (7 modified crates): clean; my edits introduce zero rustdoc warnings. (Pre-existing rustdoc breakage in sharing-server/principal.rs and filenode-server/backend.rs is unrelated and out of scope.)
- cargo fmt --all: no changes

Diff: +11 lines per crate × 7 crates = +77 lines, additive only, zero source-code or behavior changes.
